newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs end down, pork bellies settle higher.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs end down, pork bellies settle higher.

text.p: CME hog futures ended lower in response to weakness in cash hog markets and heavy commodity fund selling, and pork belly futures ended with modest gains, CME floor traders said.
"The funds were tremendous sellers in February (hogs) again today (Thursday)," one floor trader said.
Cash hogs were quoted $0.50 to $2.00 per cwt lower Thursday as weak demand for pork squeezed packer margins. Some sources expect that market to fall another $0.50 on Friday.
Demand for pork products was weak. Wholesale pork prices were steady to lower in light trade Thursday, USDA said.
"The packer is losing so much money right now that cash hogs are going to be $1.00 lower until further notice," one cash-connected source said.
Most of the buying in pork belly futures was tied to speculative short covering, traders from that pit said.
One commission house was noted buying February pork bellies and selling February hogs, a floor source said.
Refco, LIT and Merrill Lynch were all sellers of February lean hogs, traders said.
Losses in the hog futures market were trimmed by bargain hunters looking for a seasonal turnaround in hog futures, traders and analysts said.
"The price is probably right, but it's all a question of timing," a hog trader said.

CME hogs settled down 0.020 to down 0.650 cent per lb, with December down 0.350 at 54.900 cents. October hogs expired at 1200 CDT and settled down 0.225 at 54.900 cents. Pork bellies closed up 0.250 to 0.450, with February up 0.350 at 68.10.
